correctness.rationale: Verified the complete graph construction for \(q\ge2,n\ge2,1\le k\le n\). Each support necklace is a separate Eulerian strongly connected component by the n-step uniform reset. Its P spectrum has the h phase roots and remaining zeros, yielding root-independent directed tree count \(s^{a s^{k-1}-k}\). BEST and sum \(\sum a=\binom{n-1}{k-1}\) yield the stated exact global cover count. Independent integer cofactor checks for twelve parameter triples and direct Euler-tour enumeration for three small cases passed. The infinite statement rests on the written proof, not the finite experiment.

value.rationale: For the original unshortened constant-nonzero-weight language the support necklace obstruction prevents a single track in general; the minimum number and count of all optimal track families are natural exact invariants. An arbitrary-k closed product, including higher-weight components not covered by the elementary \(k=2\) case, is a useful structural enumeration. The reset-spectrum lemma explains how component tree counts depend only on the support period and primitive weight, and subsumes the classical all-nonzero de Bruijn case without merely repeating it.
